label: <DEL> step when the first two original tokens are from {w,b,0,z,e,g,m,q,o}
explanation: Fires almost only at the delimiter step (99% of activations and 99.3% of mass are at <DEL>). It is active on about 12.6% of delimiter steps, so phase==1 by itself has recall 0.99 but precision 0.13. Which delimiter steps it fires on depends on the first original tokens, i.e. the token about to be output (out_tok = orig(0)) and the one after it (next_out = orig(1)). w, b, 0, z, e, g, m, q and o give 3.5-7x lift, with w and b the strongest. orig(2) adds a weaker contribution. The effect looks additive, like a graded linear readout: the top activations (max 0.20) come from sequences that start with several w/b tokens, e.g. w b b o, b w b g. Requiring both of the first two tokens to be in the set gives precision 0.60 and recall 0.42 on dev. A weighted score over orig(0), orig(1) and orig(2) reaches F1 0.54 and mass recall 0.80. Activation is more frequent for short L (L=3: 4.2% of steps) and is also elevated at L=9. It never fires during the original phase. It fires very rarely in the copy phase (about 1%, mostly at recall_idx 1).

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the token being output (most: w, b, z, 0, e, g; least: i, v, h, x) and the second original token (most: b, 0, g, w, e, m; least: n, r, 1, x); timing cues that raise it most: phase=1, recall_idx=0, L=9 & t=10.
